newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance minister to visit Japan for loan talk.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance minister to visit Japan for loan talk.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Thursday he would visit Japan on Sunday for talks with Japanese and International Monetary Fund (IMF) officials.

Thanong said on a radio programme he would finalise a $12-15 billion IMF-sponsored austerity package for Thailand during the Tokyo visit. The minister said IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus is expected to join the talks.
Thanong said he expects the IMF board in Washington to approve the reform package by August 21 and the agency to sign the financial assistance programme with the Thai government later this month.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Thursday Japan has decided to contribute a maximum $7 billion in lending through the Export-Import Bank of Japan to a $20 billion international support package for Thailand.

It said the IMF is expected to offer $4 billion in standby credit while the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank will each put up $1 billion in medium- to long-term credit. The paper said private financial institutions including Japanese banks were prepared to put up $5 billion.

Thailand on Tuesday announced tough economic reform measures including the suspension of 42 cash-strapped finance firms, a three percentage point value added tax (VAT) hike, and hefty budget cuts after the government let the baht depreciate about 20 percent since July 2.
